chapter: Harry Parker's, the district and its characters
title: Playing at Harry Parker's in 1920 with Tinette and Keppard, and the brass ban
summary: Dawson recounts a small band at Harry Parker's with Manetta, John Vigne and violinist Tinette; brass was banned in the district until Freddie Keppard played a number under Parker's protection.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: What about somebody like Tinette? Do you remember Tinette?
Tinette, Tinette was a good musician. He was a violin player.
He was a violin player. He played, he worked with me at Harry Parker and Charlie Parker dance

I was in 19, say 1920, at Fortify. And, uh, Manetto was on the piano and I was playing guitar. John Veen on the drum. And, uh, Tinette on the violin. We didn't have no trumpet, no. I had old man Willie Umprey on the clarinet. Uh-huh. Now, at that time, they didn't allow no, uh, blowing instruments in the district there. Oh, yeah. I'm the first man that put the blowing instruments there.
No brass was allowed in there.
What, he's got piano and drums?
Piano, drums, clarinet, guitar, you know. Wow.
They used to have, they had no bass.
They used to have your small band. Yeah.

Uh, well, you see, uh, they used to dance. They had, uh, they sell liquor there, you know, they had women working there, uh, hustling. And, uh, the fellas, people would come in there. Most of the men from off the ships, they'd come in there and spend money and dance. And go on and have a good time and put, uh, we had a kiddie box that we, that dropped the money in the kiddie box for the different numbers that they want to hear, you see. And, uh, now, uh, T-Net played, uh, the last I heard of him, he played with us. And, uh, he, uh, I don't know whether he died or what. Anyway, after the fire broke out by Billy Phillips around in the middle of the block, that, uh, that killed everything. everything. So I, by me, Freddie Cap had come through there with his cornet one night and the boss asked me to see if I could get him to play a piece. So I told him no, that it was against the law. We asked Freddie if he wanted to play a number with him. He told the boss man, Harry Parker, he said, I'll play if you protect me. So Harry Parker said, well, you don't have to worry. He said, you go ahead and play a piece with Eddie and I'll see you tomorrow. I'll go to the mayor and get a permit so you can play here every night. So he did that. And from that on, Hunts and Nagel way down at the next corner, Moraes, and he had, he got the Joe Oliver's band, a whole band. What was the reason for that? They figured it was too loud? Too loud, yeah. Disturbed the piece. The loudest instrument they had was a clarinet.
